Quick data dump — pulled from usage analytics and runtime traces. Attaching cost-modeling-sheet.xlsx with numbers. Highlights: 

- Spike root cause: ~78% of additional tokens are from increased batch sizes on a small subset of endpoints (webhook pipeline) starting Sep 13 after Skylabs pushed a frontend A/B experiment that concatenates longer dialogue contexts. Not infra-induced. No model variant swap on our side in Sept.
- Latency (redwood/gpt-l-8b, prod-us-east1): p50 = 132 ms (90d avg), p95 = 412 ms (90d avg). Notable: p95 increased by ~18% since late July (coincides with higher tail queuing during peak bursts).
- Unit economics: current monthly reserve price = $28 / 1M tokens; 12-month commit recommended tier = $21 / 1M tokens (25% discount). With Skylabs' average monthly tokens (pre-spike) ~45M, moving to 12-month commit yields ~$315/mo savings; under current spike shape (avg 120M/mo) savings ~2,520/mo. Breakeven vs migration and ops overhead (estimated 6 hours of CS & infra support) ~ 2 months on their higher-usage case.
- Ops notes: enable prefix caching on the webhook route (~10-15% token reduction expected after trimming repeated system prompts). We can also suggest a light quantization profile for non-critical models (Q4 pilot) to reduce GPU cost without latency regression.

Recommendation (three options):
1) Conservative: 3-month extension with committed baseline 50M/mo + burst credits (no SLA changes).
2) Target: 12-month commit at 60M/mo (discounted $21/1M) + 5% burst lane and 99.95% latency SLO.
3) Aggressive: 12-month commit at 100M/mo + dedicated lane for peak windows (reserved GPU pool) — needs enterprise contract addendum.

Attaching: cost-modeling-sheet.xlsx for line-by-line math.

Ben
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Skylabs renewal — usage, latency, and proposed next steps (packet attached)

Hi Sofia (and Contracts team),

Thanks for the export — we've reviewed and pulled together a concise packet (attached) that summarizes root cause, perf metrics, and a 3-option commercial path. High-level summary below: 

1) What happened: the usage spike appears driven by longer dialogue contexts from your frontend A/B rollout (not a Redwood runtime change). Ben's worksheet estimates ~78% of extra tokens are attributable to the new client behavior.

2) Performance: Production p50 = 132 ms; p95 = 412 ms (90-day averages). The p95 uplift is linked to burst tail queuing during peak windows; we can reduce tail by adding a small dedicated burst lane (recommended for the aggressive option).

3) Economics: moving to a 12-month commit at $21 / 1M tokens reduces unit cost ~25%. Using current spike numbers, the incremental monthly savings would be ~ $2.5k; breakeven on migration + enablement work is ~2 months for the higher-usage scenario. See attached Skylabs_renewal_brief_v1.pdf and cost-modeling-sheet.xlsx for details.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- Skylabs: confirm preferred commercial option (Conservative | Target | Aggressive) by Sep 26.
- Redwood: assuming Target or Aggressive, we will scope the dedicated lane and prefix-caching changes; initial ETA for configs = 7 business days after contract signed.
- Contracts: if Target chosen, we'll prepare a 12-month commitment amendment (preview link: https://app.docusign.com/packets/abc123-skylabs).

Attachments included: Skylabs_renewal_brief_v1.pdf (summary + graphs), cost-modeling-sheet.xlsx (line items), and a draft MA/MP R1 doc (Skylabs_proposed_MA_MP_2028.docx).

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow (Sep 22) to walk through the packet and answer procurement questions.

Best,
Kimberly Park
